positioning.target_user: Engineers and sysadmins tailing terminal logs
positioning.job: visually distinguish consecutive command outputs in log streams
positioning.gap: no maintained free OSS alternative inserts spacers when command output stops

items.title: Add a runnable test command for gate 2 verification
items.why: Gate 1 flagged needs_test_command because no test path is visible in the repository root, causing gate 2 to stop at NEEDS_REVIEW
items.acceptance: cargo test runs successfully and exits zero in a clean checkout
items.quote: repository root: .github, .gitignore, Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml, LICENSE, README.md, images, src

items.title: Update dependencies and ensure CI passes on current Rust toolchain
items.why: The repo has working CI and a Cargo.lock but dependencies may be outdated; keeping them current reduces security and compatibility risk
items.acceptance: cargo update && cargo test passes on the latest stable Rust
items.quote: The repo has working CI (Build badge visible), is available via Homebrew and Cargo package managers, and functions as a usable CLI tool with documented usage patterns and installation scripts.

items.title: Add integration tests for the --after flag and stdin piping
items.why: The core job is a round-trip through stdin with a configurable idle timeout; automated tests prevent regressions in that behavior
items.acceptance: cargo test includes at least one integration test that pipes data, waits past --after, and asserts a spacer is emitted
items.quote: By default, `spacer` outputs a spacer after 1 second with no output. You can change this with the `--after` flag.

items.title: Support customizable separator strings
items.why: cleanlines lets users define their own separator text; adding this closes a customization gap against that alternative
items.acceptance: spacer --separator '=== NEW REQUEST ===' uses the provided string as the spacer line
items.quote: Simple bash script to clean output of the terminal and write a customazible separator.

must_beat.how_to_win: The candidate is the upstream source with active CI, Homebrew and Cargo distribution, and 1818 stars; the Alpine package is a downstream build with no independent release cadence
cleanlines is a bash script last updated in 2016 with zero stars and no license; the candidate is a maintained Rust CLI with CI, packaging, and a permissive license
tail-divider has zero stars, no license, and no packaging; the candidate adds color, file-follow, and custom separators (via UPGRADE) while retaining mature distribution channels
termseparator is a Python library with no CLI, no license, and no recent activity; the candidate is a standalone CLI with installation via Homebrew and Cargo

risks: No external demand signals beyond the repo itself (assessment:demand_evidence score 0)
No structural moat; the tool is easily replicated (assessment:moat score 0)
No clear monetization path; value remains a free CLI utility (assessment:productization_path score 1)

organised.detail: A manifest is present but no test path is visible in the root: gate 2 would stop at NEEDS_REVIEW until a test command exists.
